title: Goseong dinosaur tracksites, Jindong Formation, Korea
summary: In Goseong County, South Korea, the fluvio-lacustrine Jindong Formation preserves many track-bearing levels. Ornithopod (iguanodontid-type) trackways are most common, sauropod tracks are mostly of small individuals, theropod tracks are scarce, and bird tracks occur. The age is disputed, Albian in some work and Late Cretaceous in others. UNESCO’s tentative list cites over 4,000 footprints.

uncertainty.note: Lockley et al. (2006) report an Albian age (Lee et al.) and note a later Late Cretaceous (Santonian, potassium-argon) claim that they doubt. Bounds here are the Albian stage from the ICS chart, which may be wrong if the later dating is right.

as_recorded.value: Lee et al. (2000, 2001) continue to infer an Albian age for the Jindong Formation
Paik et al. (2001) suggest that the formation is Late Cretaceous in age

when.display: Albian by one view (c. 113 to 100.5 Ma); age disputed

where.modern_name: Deongmyeong-ri, Hai-myeon, Goseong-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do, South Korea
where.historical_name: Jindong Formation, Gyeongsang Basin (intra-arc lake and river basin), Cretaceous; no polities exist

importance.justification: A very large dinosaur and bird footprint record, much of the vertebrate evidence for the Korean Mesozoic.

sources.title: Dinosaur-dominated footprint assemblages from the Cretaceous Jindong Formation, Hallyo Haesang National Park area, Goseong County, South Korea: Evidence and implications
sources.author: M.G. Lockley et al.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the age (Albian vs Late Cretaceous) and of the pin: UNESCO gives Deongmyeong-ri in degrees and minutes for one of several Goseong sites. Both pages were read through the Wayback Machine because the originals are gone or blocked. No animation, since the age is disputed.
